questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reason for the highest boiling point of R-COOH as compared to alkanes, ethers, alcohols and aldehydes.
options: Van der waals force of attraction
questions.solution:
Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alkanes, ethers, alcohols, and aldehydes of comparable molecular mass.

This is due to the presence of strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding in carboxylic acids. The highly polarized O-H bond, enhanced by the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group, allows carboxylic acid molecules to form strong hydrogen bonds with each other. Because of this extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding, they often exist as dimers even in the vapor phase or in non-polar solvents, requiring more energy to separate the molecules during boiling.

Answer: Formation of intermolecular hydrogen bonding

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the reagent used in following reaction.
$\text{Benzoic acid} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\large{\text{Reagent}}} \text{Benzoyl chloride} + \text{phosphorous oxychloride} + \text{Hydrogen chloride}$
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzoic acid with phosphorus pentachloride ($\text{PCl}_5$) yields benzoyl chloride, phosphorus oxychloride ($\text{POCl}_3$), and hydrogen chloride ($\text{HCl}$).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} + \text{PCl}_5 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$

Thus, the reagent used is $\text{PCl}_5$.

Answer: $\text{PCl}_5$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following is NOT a monocarboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
Toluic acid is methylbenzoic acid, which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Acrylic acid is propenoic acid (CH_2=CH-COOH$), which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Phthalic acid is benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid (C_6H_4(COOH)_2$), which contains two $-COOH$ groups. Thus, it is a dicarboxylic acid.

Isobutyric acid is 2-methylpropanoic acid ($(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$), which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Therefore, phthalic acid is not a monocarboxylic acid.

Answer: Phthalic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when isopropyl magnesium chloride in dry ether reacts with dry ice forming a complex, hydrolysed further.
questions.solution:
Isopropyl magnesium chloride is $(CH_3)_2CHMgCl$.

Dry ice is solid $CO_2$.

When a Grignard reagent reacts with dry ice, it undergoes nucleophilic addition to the carbonyl group of $CO_2$ to form a magnesium carboxylate complex.

$(CH_3)_2CHMgCl + O=C=O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl$

Upon acid hydrolysis, the complex yields a carboxylic acid.

$(CH_3)_2CH-COOMgCl + H_2O \rightarrow (CH_3)_2CH-COOH + Mg(OH)Cl$

The product $(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$ is 2-methylpropanoic acid.

Answer: 2 - Methylpropanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify final products in the following sequence of reactions
$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}^+}} \text{intermediate} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{Ni}, \Delta}}^{\large{\text{H}_2}} \text{Products}$
questions.solution:
The first step is the Fischer esterification reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst. The reaction produces an ester as the intermediate.

$\text{RCOOH} + \text{R'OH} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{RCOOR'} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The intermediate formed is the ester $\text{RCOOR'}$.

The second step involves the catalytic hydrogenation (hydrogenolysis) of the ester using hydrogen gas over a nickel catalyst at high temperature. This process cleaves the ester bond, reducing the acyl group ($\text{RCO}-$) to a primary alcohol and releasing the alkoxy group ($-\text{OR'}$) as another alcohol.

$\text{RCOOR'} + 2\text{H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}, \Delta} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'OH}$

Thus, the final products are $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{R'OH}$.

Answer: $\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} + \text{R'}-\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the main product of following reaction
questions.solution:
DIBAL-H (Diisobutylaluminium hydride) is a selective reducing agent.

It reduces esters and nitriles to aldehydes.

The reaction proceeds as follows:
$\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{O}-\text{R}' \xrightarrow[\text{2. H}_3\text{O}^+]{\text{1. DIBAL-H}} \text{R}-\text{CHO} + \text{R}'-\text{OH}$

Therefore, the main product is an aldehyde, $\text{RCHO}$.

Answer: $\text{RCHO}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When will be the acidic character of carboxylic acid higher in following cases ?
questions.solution:
Acidic strength of a carboxylic acid is directly proportional to its acid dissociation constant $K_a$.

Higher the value of $K_a$, stronger is the acid.

The relationship between $pK_a$ and $K_a$ is given by $pK_a = -\log K_a$.

Thus, a higher value of $K_a$ corresponds to a lower value of $pK_a$.

Therefore, higher acidic character corresponds to a higher $K_a$ value and a lower $pK_a$ value.

Answer: Higher $K_a$ value and lower $pK_a$ value

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When sodium bicarbonate is added to an organic compound, brisk effervescences is evolved. This indicate the presence of which functional group.
questions.solution:
Sodium bicarbonate ($NaHCO_3$) is a weak base that reacts with compounds more acidic than carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$).

Carboxylic acids ($-\text{COOH}$) react with sodium bicarbonate to produce sodium carboxylate, water, and carbon dioxide gas.

The reaction is given by:

$R-\text{COOH} + NaHCO_3 \rightarrow R-\text{COONa} + H_2O + CO_2 \uparrow$

The evolution of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) gas is observed as brisk effervescence. This test is the standard qualitative test used to detect the presence of the carboxylic acid functional group in an organic compound.

Answer: $-\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the common name for the simplest carboxylic acid, HCOOH ?
questions.solution:
The simplest carboxylic acid is $HCOOH$.

Its IUPAC name is methanoic acid.

Its common name is formic acid, derived from the Latin word 'formica' meaning ant, as it was first isolated from the destructive distillation of ants.

Answer: Formic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest carboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
The acidic strength of carboxylic acids depends on the stability of the conjugate base (carboxylate ion).

Electron-withdrawing groups (EWG) stabilize the conjugate base through the $-I$ effect, thereby increasing the acidic strength. Electron-donating groups (EDG) destabilize the conjugate base through the $+I$ effect, decreasing the acidic strength.

In the given options:
$\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ has a $-\text{Cl}$ group which exerts a strong $-I$ effect.
$\text{HCOOH}$ has a hydrogen atom (reference for $I$ effect).
$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ has a $-\text{CH}_3$ group which exerts a $+I$ effect.
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ has an ethyl group which exerts a stronger $+I$ effect than the methyl group.

Due to the strong $-I$ effect of the chlorine atom, the chloroacetate ion is the most stable conjugate base. Thus, $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ is the strongest acid.

Answer: $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which is a weakest acid among the following ?
questions.solution:
Acidic strength is directly proportional to the stability of the conjugate base.

Electron-withdrawing groups ($-I$ effect) stabilize the carboxylate ion and increase acidic strength, while electron-donating groups ($+I$ effect) destabilize the carboxylate ion and decrease acidic strength.

The $+I$ effect of the isopropyl group $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-$ is greater than that of the methyl group $\text{CH}_3-$.

Chlorine atoms exert a $-I$ effect, which increases acidic strength. Thus, $\text{Cl}_3\text{CCOOH}$ and $\text{ClCH}_2\text{COOH}$ are stronger acids.

Since $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-$ has the maximum $+I$ effect among the given groups, it destabilizes the conjugate base the most, making $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$ the weakest acid.

Answer: $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following species is used in Friedel - Craft reaction?
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts acylation is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction where an acyl group is introduced into an aromatic ring. The reagents typically used for this reaction are acyl halides (such as acid chlorides, $R-CO-Cl$) or acid anhydrides, in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst like anhydrous $AlCl_3$.

Among the given options, $R-CO-Cl$ (acid chloride) is the correct species used in the Friedel-Crafts acylation reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is dicarboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
To identify the dicarboxylic acid, we examine the carboxyl group count for each compound.

Valeric acid (pentanoic acid) has formula $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$, containing one carboxyl group and is thus monocarboxylic.

Caproic acid (hexanoic acid) is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}$, also monocarboxylic.

Glutaric acid (pentanedioic acid) has structure $\text{HOOC}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$, with two carboxyl groups, making it dicarboxylic.

Butyric acid (butanoic acid) is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$, again monocarboxylic.

The dicarboxylic acid is glutaric acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify product obtained when acyl chloride undergoes hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of acyl chlorides proceeds through nucleophilic acyl substitution, with water acting as the nucleophile. The general reaction is $RCOCl + H_2O \rightarrow RCOOH + HCl$.

A tetrahedral intermediate forms when the oxygen atom of water attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Proton transfer occurs, and chloride acts as the leaving group. The carbonyl group reforms, yielding the carboxylic acid.

The product is therefore a carboxylic acid.

$\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{Mg} \mathrm{Br} \xrightarrow[\text{ ii) dil. } \mathrm{HCl}]{$$\text{ i) Dry ice/ dry ether }$$} $$\text{ Product }$
questions.solution:
Grignard Reaction with Carbon Dioxide

Ethylmagnesium bromide ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{MgBr}$) reacts as a nucleophile with carbon dioxide ($\mathrm{CO}_2$) in dry ether, attacking the electrophilic carbon to form a magnesium carboxylate salt.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{MgBr} + \mathrm{CO}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{Mg}^{+}\mathrm{Br}$

Hydrolysis with dilute hydrochloric acid liberates the carboxylic acid.

$\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{Mg}^{+}\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{MgBrCl}$

The product is propanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{COOH}$), corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Find the number of moles of glycerol produced when n mole of triglyceride undergoes saponification.
questions.solution:
The saponification reaction involves hydrolysis of the ester linkage in triglycerides using a strong base. A triglyceride consists of one glycerol molecule esterified with three fatty acid chains.

$\text{Triglyceride} + 3\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Glycerol} + 3\text{RCOONa}$

From stoichiometry, each mole of triglyceride yields exactly one mole of glycerol. With $n$ moles of triglyceride reacting, the glycerol produced must also be $n$ moles.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{A}}$

questions.solution:
Benzoyl chloride is hydrolyzed by water to benzoic acid via nucleophilic acyl substitution.

The reaction $\mathrm{C_6 H_5 COCl + H_2 O \rightarrow C_6 H_5 COOH + HCl}$ occurs directly, as acid chlorides readily undergo hydrolysis with H₂O.

Chromium trioxide and potassium permanganate are oxidizing agents unsuitable for this transformation.

While dilute sodium hydroxide yields the carboxylate salt initially, water provides the most direct route to the carboxylic acid.

In a reaction,

The Grignard reagent isopropyl magnesium bromide, $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CHMgBr}$, undergoes carboxylation with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ in dry ether to form a magnesium carboxylate intermediate.

$\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHMgBr} + \mathrm{CO}_2 \to \left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHCOO}^- \mathrm{MgBr}^+$

Hydrolysis with dilute $\mathrm{HCl}$ yields the carboxylic acid product.

$\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHCOO}^- \mathrm{MgBr}^+ + \mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{O}^+ \to \left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_2\mathrm{CHCOOH} + \mathrm{Mg}^{2+} + \mathrm{Br}^- + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$

The $\mathrm{IUPAC}$ name of $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CHCOOH}$ is 2-methylpropanoic acid, corresponding to option B.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following functional groups is reduced by diborane?
questions.solution:
Diborane ($B_2 H_6$) reduces the following functional groups:

Esters ($\mathrm{-COOR}$) are reduced to primary alcohols: $RCOOR' \xrightarrow{B_2 H_6} RCH_2 OH + R'OH$.

Carboxylic acids ($\mathrm{-COOH}$) are reduced to primary alcohols: $RCOOH \xrightarrow{B_2 H_6} RCH_2 OH$. Diborane is particularly useful for selective reduction of carboxylic acids.

Nitro groups ($\mathrm{-NO_2}$) are reduced to primary amines: $RNO_2 \xrightarrow{B_2 H_6} RNH_2$.

Alkyl halides ($\mathrm{-X}$) are unreactive toward diborane under typical conditions.

Therefore, options A, B, and C are reduced by diborane.

$\boxed{\text{A, B, C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If salicylic acid (138 u) reacts with acetic anhydride (102 u) to from aspirin (180 u) calculate % atom economy
questions.solution:
The atom economy is calculated as the ratio of the molecular mass of the desired product to the total molecular mass of all reactants, expressed as a percentage.

Given the molecular masses: aspirin (desired product) = 180 u, salicylic acid = 138 u, and acetic anhydride = 102 u, the sum of reactant masses is $138 + 102 = 240$ u.

Substituting into the formula yields $\frac{180}{240} \times 100\% = 0.75 \times 100\% = 75\%$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following is dicarboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
To identify the dicarboxylic acid, we examine the carboxyl group count for each compound.

Valeric acid (pentanoic acid) has formula $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$, containing one carboxyl group and is thus monocarboxylic.

Caproic acid (hexanoic acid) is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\text{COOH}$, also monocarboxylic.

Glutaric acid (pentanedioic acid) has structure $\text{HOOC}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{COOH}$, with two carboxyl groups, making it dicarboxylic.

Butyric acid (butanoic acid) is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{COOH}$, again monocarboxylic.

The dicarboxylic acid is glutaric acid.

questions.q: Which of the following reactions involves $\alpha$ -halogenation of carboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
Hell Volhard Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction:
This reaction involves alpha bromination of carboxylic acids. Carboxylic acids react with chlorine or bromine in presence of small amount of red phosphorous to give alpha halo carboxylic acids.
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH} \stackrel{\mathrm{Br}_{2} / \mathrm{P}}{\rightarrow} \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{COOH} \stackrel{\mathrm{Br}_{2} / \mathrm{P}}{\rightarrow} \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CBr}_{2}-$
$\mathrm{COOH} \stackrel{\mathrm{Br}_{2} / \mathrm{P}}{\longrightarrow}$ No further reaction.
